# Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts

## Problem statement

The audit SCANNING blocks and docs currently recommend
`scan.py find-workitem <id>` for worklog lookups (wired in by
SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1; guidance refined by SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI).
`scan.py find-workitem` wraps `wl search <id> --json` plus an exact-id
post-filter. Once the wl CLI gains tolerant ID resolution (the ContextHub
feature below), audit agents should use native wl commands for worklog
lookups and `scan.py find-workitem` can be retired.

## Blocked by

- **WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E** — "Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to `wl show`
  (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool
  use" — feature request in the **ContextHub** repository
  (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), created 2026-08-11.

This item MUST NOT start until that feature lands in the installed wl CLI
(the exact-match `wl show` today cannot resolve partial/truncated IDs, which
is why the scan.py wrapper exists). Cross-project dependency — recorded here
as a blocker; not a `wl dep` edge (different worklog DBs).

## Substring-matching guidance (researched — use ONLY the optimal command)

The canonical substring-matching primitive is **`wl list <term> --json`**:
case-insensitive substring match over id/title/description, JSON mode returns
all matches, supports `-n/--number` and filters (see `src/commands/list.ts`
in ContextHub).

`wl search <keywords> --json` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) —
**not** a substring matcher — and must NOT be presented as one.

Exact / unique-ID resolution: **`wl show <id> --json`** (tolerant once
WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E lands; `scan.py find-workitem <id>` interim).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All SCANNING blocks in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_PHASE1_SCANNING_BLOCK`, phase2_child, phase2_batch, phase2_deep) direct
   worklog lookups to native wl commands only:
   - substring matching: `wl list <term> --json`
   - exact/unique-ID resolution: `wl show <id> --json`
2. The dual recommendation "`wl search <keywords> --json` or
   `wl list <term> --json` for substring matching" (introduced by
   SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI) is corrected to the single optimal command
   **`wl list <term> --json`** everywhere it appears (audit_runner.py +
   docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md), per the research note above.
3. `scan.py find-workitem` is removed (subcommand, its tests, and references
   in audit-grep-scan-patterns.md) OR deprecated with a clear notice — the
   decision is documented in a comment; `scan.py search-code` and
   `scan.py list-files` remain unchanged.
4. docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md
   (incl. the P9 replacement recipe) updated to the native commands.
5. Full project test suite passes (canonical PATH with `~/.local/bin`).
6. Related docs (README, wiki/docs-site entries, code comments, scan.py
   module docstring) updated; no stale `scan.py find-workitem` guidance
   remains.

## Out of scope

- No changes to `scan.py search-code` / `list-files` (bounded code search).
- No changes to the wl CLI itself — tracked in ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E.
- No changes to audit verdict semantics or prompt structure beyond the
  worklog-lookup guidance lines.

## Related work

- SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI — removed stale `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` grep
  guidance from audit prompts (completed, this item's precursor).
- SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1 — wired scan.py guidance into audit prompts (the
  guidance this item replaces).
- SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM / SA-0MSBSOAEM0078LAO — scan hygiene parents.
data.title: Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts (blocked by ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E)

# Test: invert launch-context guard assertions

**Parent:** SA-0MSRLECW2001AA15 — Audit runner: make TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT per-audit dynamic

## Goal

Invert the existing `TestLaunchContextGuard` abort-on-mismatch tests so they assert that a determinable non-owning cwd launch proceeds (with a one-line stderr warning) and that only undeterminable ownership aborts with zero git commands and zero pi calls.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `test_non_owning_cwd_aborts_with_zero_pi_calls` is rewritten to assert that a non-owning cwd proceeds (rc == 0, pi calls are made) and that a one-line stderr warning naming launch vs owning root is emitted.
2. `test_non_owning_cwd_error_names_resolved_vs_expected` is rewritten: no more `Audit launch-context error` — instead assert the stderr contains a warning with both roots.
3. `test_undeterminable_ownership_aborts` is verified/updated: undeterminable ownership (no --worklog-dir, unknown prefix, no sibling match) still aborts with non-zero exit, zero pi calls, and the `Undeterminable project scope` error message.
4. `test_explicit_worklog_dir_does_not_bypass_wrong_cwd` is rewritten: an explicit --worklog-dir from a non-owning cwd now proceeds (it is determinable ownership, just a different cwd).
5. `test_owning_cwd_passes_guard_and_runs_unchanged` is verified unchanged: owning cwd still passes cleanly (no warning).
6. `test_guard_runs_before_any_wl_status_transition` is updated: guard no longer fires before status transition for determinable launches; only undeterminable launches abort before any wl status change.
7. `TestGitResolutionFromNonOwningCwd` tests are extended to assert that the per-audit root is threaded correctly to all consumers (code-quality scan, debug-log dir, remediation loop, F3 suite-execution cwd).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` — `TestLaunchContextGuard`, `TestGitResolutionFromNonOwningCwd`

## Dependencies

None — this task reads the current test state and the implementation change simultaneously.

# Problem

All 10 planning/analysis/maintenance skills use placeholder `--ac` values in their final-step `render_report` blocks. Agents therefore pass the work item's feature ACs (unmet pre-implementation), causing the report to show "incomplete" when the skill session actually completed.

SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5 made `render_report()` derive session status from AC verdicts: any unmet → "incomplete". SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z fixed intake by passing concrete process-deliverable ACs. This child fixes the remaining 10 skills.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each SKILL.md's final-step `--ac` block replaced with concrete skill-session deliverable ACs (4 per skill for skills with multiple deliverables; 3 for simpler skills).
2. Each final-step block includes a one-line note: "> **Note:** ACs record the *skill session's* own deliverables — not the work item's feature acceptance criteria."
3. No code changes — SKILL.md docs only.
4. Full test suite green (existing tests unaffected by doc-only changes).
5. No new `--ac` lines change the renderer's behaviour; all `--ac` values use the "met" verdict on success.

## Skills affected

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: plan approved, children created, ACs traceable.
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: keyword derivation, wl search, repo file search, summary compiled.
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: PERT estimate computed, risk score assessed, confidence stated, WBS suggested.
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: test failures parsed, critical items triaged, work items created/linked.
- `skill/author-command/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: command spec drafted, SKILL.md written, script stub created, tests written.
- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: branches assessed, stale branches pruned, orphaned stashes triaged, comments posted.
- `skill/code-review/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: code quality analysis run, findings documented, recommendations provided.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: code smells detected, refactoring plan drafted, changes applied.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: machine pressure assessed, safe remediations proposed, actions logged.
- `skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: PR comments fetched, fixes proposed, threads resolved after approval.

## Risks

- Adding `--ac` lines to each SKILL.md is a mechanical but widespread change. Mitigation: each change is independent and reversible.
- If a skill's final-step block is very long, adding ACs + note might make it verbose. Mitigation: ACs are concise (40–60 chars each).

## Related

- **SA-0MUUI6ZCX001RO8V** — Epic (parent).
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — Renderer conditional header/conclusion.
- **SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z** — Intake SKILL.md fix (sibling, in_review).
- **SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR** — Adds "Use Cases" section for work-item ACs.

# Problem

The 4 operational/delivery skills (test, ship, implement, audit) use placeholder `--ac` values. For test/ship the session ACs are the operational deliverables (suite run, failures triaged / release promoted, audit performed). For implement/audit, the semantics are different — these skills evaluate the work item's ACs as part of their session, which is a legitimate use of `--ac`. This child clarifies the distinction and aligns with SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **test** (`skill/test/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block replaced with 4 skill-session ACs: full test suite executed, failures parsed into triage records, critical failures triaged into work items, report rendered.
2. **ship** (`skill/ship/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block replaced with 4 skill-session ACs: dev-to-main merge performed, audit comment posted, operator notified, CHANGELOG updated.
3. **implement** (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block updated with skill-session ACs: worktree created, tests written/updated, build green, tests green, commit made, push to dev. **Note added:** "For implement, the work-item feature ACs are evaluated during execution but are not passed to `render_report` — the report records the implement session's own success criteria. Work-item ACs are displayed in the Use Cases section (SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR)."
4. **audit** (`skill/audit/SKILL.md`): `--ac` block updated with skill-session ACs: work item assessed, audit verdict determined, Ready to close line added. **Note added:** "For audit, the verdict reflects the work item's state; the report records the audit session's own success criteria (audit was performed). Work-item ACs are displayed in the Use Cases section (SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR)."
5. No code changes — SKILL.md docs only.
6. Full test suite green.

## Skills affected

- `skill/test/SKILL.md`
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`

## Risks

- **Implement/audit semantics**: these skills legitimately evaluate work-item ACs. The note clarifies that the report's `--ac` table still records session success (not work-item status), and work-item ACs go in the Use Cases section.
- If SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR ("Use Cases" section) is not yet implemented, the notes reference it as a dependency.

## Related

- **SA-0MUUI6ZCX001RO8V** — Epic (parent).
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — Renderer conditional header/conclusion.
- **SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z** — Intake SKILL.md fix (sibling).
- **SA-0MTQY7YM5009J6QR** — Adds "Use Cases" section for work-item ACs.

# Problem

There is no automated guard against future regressions of the placeholder-`--ac` pattern. Agents adding new report-rendering skills (or editing existing ones) might again use `--ac "<AC# description>|…|met"` placeholders instead of concrete skill-session deliverables.

SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S already added `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` which checks that every work-item skill has the final-step section and invokes `render_report`. This child extends it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Extend `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` with a new test class `TestReportACConcreteness`:
   - `test_all_final_step_acs_are_concrete`: asserts each work-item skill's `--ac` lines contain at least one literal `|met` value (no placeholders like `<AC# description>`).
   - `test_all_final_steps_have_semantics_note`: asserts each work-item skill's final-step block contains a note distinguishing skill-session ACs from work-item feature ACs (search for patterns like "skill session" or "own deliverable" in the final-step block).
2. Add the new test class to the existing test file (no new test files).
3. All 6 existing hygiene tests still pass.
4. Full test suite green.

## Tests

- `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` — extended with `TestReportACConcreteness` (2 new tests).

## Skills covered

The test covers all 15 skills in `WORK_ITEM_SKILLS` (audit, author-command, cleanup, code-review, effort-and-risk, find-related, implement, intake, machine-hygiene, plan, refactor, resolve-pr-comments, ship, test, triage).

## Related

- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — Original report helper work (existing hygiene test).

## Broader scope + final fix

The same root cause (fixtures omitting the newly-added `llm.js`) affected four temp-fixture tests, not just one:

- `tests/unit/test-code-freeze-marker.mjs`
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-arg-filtering.mjs`
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`
- `tests/unit/test-run-release.mjs`

Each copies `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` (which now imports `./llm.js`) into a `mkdtemp` skill dir but did not copy `llm.js`, so `run-release.js`'s import chain failed in the temp dir (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND / empty argv forwarded to the merge script).

**Fix:** copy `llm.js` alongside `timing.js` in every affected fixture.

**Verification:** `node --test tests/unit/**/*.mjs` → 659/659 pass; `node --test tests/unit/test-code-freeze-marker.mjs` → 11/11.

Delivered on branch `wl-SA-0MUWKGW9W004QXQZ-...` at commit `b1246db3` (pushed to dev together with the parent fix).
